title: The keep
description: The keep is a fourteen-day fortnight a person carries from their planner app to the web: what is eaten and what is booked, keyed by day key and carrying no dates. This is its machine schema. The canonical copy lives with the format's specification (docs/keep-format.md); a byte-identical copy travels with the app that writes keeps. Edit the canonical one - the copies are compared and any difference is reported as drift. TWO BARS, and this schema is the higher one: a CONFORMING keep is complete and well-formed, which is what this file certifies; a READABLE keep is merely one a page can draw something from, which is a lower bar the reader applies. A hand-maker mid-draft sits between the two on purpose. OPEN BY CONSTRUCTION: no object here sets additionalProperties to false, because adding a field is not a version bump - the app and the website ship on different cadences, and the person holding the phone cannot redeploy the website, so a reader must ignore what it does not know and refuse only a HIGHER version. A future per-member section would be additive in exactly this way and would need no bump.

meta.description: What the file is, and when it was made.

format.description: Renamed from "myfort" on 2026-08-28 as a clean break; the version stayed 1 under the new name.

version.description: Bumped only for a breaking change. A reader refuses a HIGHER version and tolerates unknown fields at the same one.

exportedAt.description: When the file was written. Null is legitimate: the writer takes this as an argument and defaults it to null, so a caller that omits a clock produces null rather than omitting the key. The fourteen days carry no dates and never go stale; only the season and year snapshots age.

days.description: Exactly the canonical fourteen, each once, in canonical order. The fourteen day keys are the format's skeleton, not household vocabulary - the fortnight is the product. NOTE: this schema pins the count and the vocabulary; that each key appears exactly once and in order is a rule of the specification that JSON Schema cannot express, and is enforced by test instead.

label.description: The day's name as the household writes it. Rendered verbatim.

blocks.description: The day's blocks in order. Block keys are household vocabulary, not a fixed set - one household's day runs early/midday/late/too-dark, another's need not - so they are not enumerated here.

focus.description: The workbook's display text, not a category key. Null where the block carries none.

meal.description: The meal this block carries, or null. An object - not a string.

meals.description: The day's three dishes, or null when the day carries none.

appointments.description: The recurring ideal week - what is booked in principle, not the device's real calendar.

menu.description: The fortnight menu, grouped by meal slot: which dish is cooked on which day, and which later day eats it as leftovers. ABSENT IS NOT EMPTY: a keep written before 2026-08-29 has no menu section at all, which says the export predates menus; a menu present but empty says the household has none. Tooling that reports on a keep must say which it saw. Meal keys and dish text are the household's own words and are never enumerated or normalised.

label.description: The slot's display name, rendered verbatim. Today's writer emits Brunch/Snack/Dinner; a household with its own words for its meals may write its own.

entries.description: The dishes in this slot across the fortnight. About eight dishes cover fourteen days: most are eaten twice, the second time as leftovers.

mealKey.description: The household's own id for the dish within its slot. Not enumerated.

menu.description: The dish, in the household's words.

cookDay.description: The day the dish is cooked.

leftoversDay.description: The day it is eaten again, or null when it is eaten once.

cookExtra.description: Cook more than the two servings need: the surplus is an ingredient in a later dish.

cookExtraNote.description: Why, in the household's words. Free text, and the only prose the menu sends to a page.

season.description: A snapshot of the season current when the file was exported, or null when no season resolved. Season ids are one household's vocabulary and are never enumerated.

mealIdeas.description: Emitted by the writer; absent from both published fixtures, which is why it is documented here rather than inferred from an example.

year.description: The year wheel, or null. Non-null only when a season resolved and the wheel covers a year.

slices.description: The wheel's slices in the order they are drawn. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: season colours come from a positional palette pinned to a slice's first appearance here, never to a household's season ids, so re-exporting cannot shift them.
